{{Short description|Generalization of a topos in mathematics}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically [[category theory]], a '''quasitopos''' is a generalization of a [[topos]]. A topos has a [[subobject classifier]] classifying all subobjects, but in a quasitopos, only strong subobjects are classified. Quasitoposes are also required to be [[complete category|finitely cocomplete]] and locally cartesian closed.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7Cj9N7ctjl8C|title=Lecture Notes on Topoi and Quasitopoi|last=Wyler|first=Oswald|isbn=978-9810201531|access-date=3 February 2017|year=1991}}</ref> A solid quasitopos is one for which 0 is a strong subobject of 1.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Quasitopoi, logic and heyting-valued models|journal=[[Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra]]|volume=42|issue=2|pages=141–164|last=Monro|first=G.P.|date=September 1986|doi=10.1016/0022-4049(86)90077-0 | doi-access=free}}</ref>
